question: is the declared runtime bound 'Dart VM service' reachable from the artifact a Flutter release build produces, or only from a profile-mode build?
method: build both modes from one pinned revision of one real campaign application, install each on a reset AVD, launch it, and read the Dart VM service announcement out of that launch's own logcat window

application.preparation: sh scripts/remove_proprietary_dependencies.sh run under debian:bookworm-slim, because the script uses GNU sed -i and silently leaves a broken tree when run with BSD sed on macOS

device.note: no x86_64 Android system image exists on this host, so the measurement ran on arm64-v8a. The measurement is about the build mode, not the architecture, but the architecture is recorded because the target's declared arch bound is x86_64

runs.logcat: I flutter : The Dart VM service is listening on http://127.0.0.1:38635/1X8DUVPoS6I=/
no Dart VM service, Observatory, or Dart VM line appears in the launch's logcat window
runs.signing: a throwaway keystore generated inside the work directory, so no upstream secret was needed

result.statement: the release APK of a real campaign application starts and runs, and publishes no Dart VM service. The declared runtime bound is reachable from a profile-mode build only
result.consequence: a flutter-android campaign observes profile-mode builds, and the support claim must say so. The runtime bound is restated as 'Dart VM service (profile-mode build)' rather than left to imply that a shipped release APK is observable

cargokit resolves rustup under $HOME/.cargo while the worker image keeps the toolchain in /usr/local, which fails as 'rustup is not installed at /root/.cargo'
